subject: Orchestrion capacity: throughput forecast & headroom reconciliation
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Rivers <ben.rivers@orchestrion.ai>, Alice Chen <alice@orchestrion.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial capacity sketch — T/sec targets & SLO fit

Hi Ben / Alice,

Thanks again for the call earlier. Per our discussion, I put together a short sketch of how we see Orchestrion's committed slab mapping to tokens/sec and SLA headroom. This is intentionally conservative to make room for burst and model upgrades. A few highlights below — full numbers attached in the spreadsheet (orch_compute_model.xlsx).

Summary assumptions:
- Primary model: llama-3-70b-q4 (production), quantized variant for cost (approx. 1.9x throughput vs fp16).
- Baseline p95 latency target: 600 ms for 8k-context generation workloads (your SLO).
- Peak user concurrency estimate from your team: 1.8k concurrent sessions during morning peak (per Ben).

Quick band math (ballpark):
- Measured tokens/sec per A100-v4 (w/ q4 path, dynamic batching): ~2200 tokens/sec sustained for 8k average sequences.
- Effective tokens/sec per slab unit (1 slab = 8xA100-v4): ~17.6k tokens/sec sustained.
- For a committed token run-rate of 420M tokens/day (~4.86k tps average), recommended reserved slab: 1 slab with burst buffer for morning peaks (can sustain ~120k tps short bursts across pool with autoscale).

Headroom & SLO mapping:
- To meet p95 600ms under 1.8k concurrent sessions with typical prompt sizes, we recommend 35% safety factor above projected sustained TPS to preserve tail latency during cold starts and KV cache misses.
- With 1 slab + 35% buffer we estimate p95 headroom for typical peak distributions; full sensitivity is in the sheet.

Ask: can you confirm two pieces so we can lock the sizing and commercial recommendation?
1) Typical request size distribution: fraction of requests that go >1k tokens (long generations).
2) Quiet hours / regional skew: do you have a >2x concentration in US-East mornings or is traffic spread across PST/EST equally?

Attached: initial SLA draft and compute model. Monica — can you add ops notes on warmup/KV caching?

Thanks,
Sean
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Sean — this is helpful. A few quick answers from our side:

- Request size: roughly 65% of calls are short (<200 tokens), ~25% mid (200–800 tokens), ~10% long (>800 tokens). Long requests skew the GPU memory pressure and KV cache usage.
- Regional skew: most of our users are US-based; morning peak is PST heavy (roughly 60% of peak in PST window), with a smaller EST bump. No APAC traffic for now.
- Procurement timeline: procurement@orchestrion.ai will start review next Tuesday. We need a committed plan by June 10 if possible.

Couple of questions:
1) What is your recommended steady committed slab if we want 99.9% availability and p95 latency at 600ms, assuming the distribution above?
2) How do outages / GPU failures get handled in the Dedicated tier — do you have transparent fallback to a slightly cheaper model variant?

We will loop procurement in as the next step.

—Ben
VP Product, Orchestrion

On Thu, May 21, 2026 at 08:03 AM Ben Rivers <ben.rivers@orchestrion.ai> wrote:
> What is your recommended steady committed slab if we want 99.9% availability and p95 latency at 600ms, assuming the distribution above?

Hi Ben — quick ops note. I'm attaching the compute model but also pasting the short answer below (ops-mode):

Recommended steady-state (ops rationale):
- Sustained baseline: 1 slab (8xA100-v4) sized to cover the sustained token run-rate driven primarily by mid/short calls. That matches Sean's baseline.
- Peak & redundancy: Reserve an additional 0.5 slab equivalent as hot-standby/burst capacity (we manage as reserved slack + autoscale headroom). This gets you to ~1.5 slab effective capacity which covers the 1.8k concurrent morning peak under the 65/25/10 mix with p95 ~550–650ms in our internal sim if KV cache hit-rate stays >80%.
- Failure handling: Dedicated instances are configured with fast re-routing (service mesh + model variant fallback). If a physical GPU node fails, we spill to warmed secondary nodes and automatically route to the nearest compatible quantized variant with slightly higher latency (p95 + ~120–200ms) until we heal.

Ops tuning knobs to preserve p95:
- Warmup: pre-warm caches for predicted top 10 prompts to raise KV hit-rate during morning ramp.
- Batching window: 6–10ms dynamic window for mid-volume periods, tighten to 3–5ms at low latency-sensitive endpoints.
- Quantized rollback policy: maintain a canary pool (2–4 nodes) running the primary fp16 model; fall back to q4 only for non-SLA critical routes.

I'll add the street-level simulation numbers to the spreadsheet (orch_compute_model.xlsx) — look at the "sensitivity" tab.

—Monica
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Ben — following up after Monica's ops numbers. Quick commercial + sizing recommendation that ties to procurement timelines:

Sizing recommendation (final):
- Commit: 1 slab reserved (8xA100-v4) for steady state.
- Safety/avail: Add 0.5 slab equivalent as part of reserved agreement (we model this as a priority burst pool) — commercial effective capacity = 1.5 slab.
- Short-term burst: Autoscale pool to allow short bursts up to 3x sustained for <5 minute windows.

Why 1.5 slab: gives ~35–40% headroom against forecasted afternoon/morning peaks while preserving p95 SLA with the request mix you described. It also buys room for a canary rollout of fp16 model nodes without disrupting production traffic.

Commercial notes / timeline:
- If we sign commitment by June 10, we can lock current pricing and start a two-week warmup + canary window to validate tail latency before your June 30 go-live.
- Kimberly — discount cadence and draft MOU are with you; recommend a 6% commit discount for a 12-month reserved term with a single mid-year true-up.

Next steps:
1) Ben/procurement to confirm acceptance of 1.5 slab effective commitment by June 10.
2) We'll schedule a technical kickoff (Monica) to walk the canary warmup plan next week.
3) Kimberly will send MOU + procurement checklist.

Sean
